subject: w547/GAUSSIAN_BOUNDARY.md#C002
independent_reproduction: Angular averages of both sin^2 and cos^2 are pi; the radial 1/k term gives coefficient |G|^2/(4pi) log r. For p<2 the longitudinal spectral integral is L1 and tends to |G|^2 Lambda^(2-p)/(4pi(2-p)). Curl kills P_L and has density T/(4mu); disk integration gives Var(theta)=T Lambda^2/(16pi mu), hence the sixfold pair limit exp[-36 Var(theta)]=exp[-9T Lambda^2/(4pi mu)].
gap: No justified microscopic p(s) map; no free dislocations or actual bond-orientational observable.

subject: w547/GAUSSIAN_BOUNDARY.md#C003
scope: fixed-p Gaussian asymptotic and endpoint continuity
independent_reproduction: For p<2 the longitudinal term has a finite r->infinity limit, so its log-r coefficient is zero. At p=2 its coefficient is T|G|^2/(4pi a). For fixed r, 1-cos(k.re)=O(k^2) provides a p-independent integrable majorant near k=0, so p->2- can precede r->infinity. The iterated limits differ by T|G|^2/(4pi a)>0.
gap: This is a Gaussian endpoint warning, not a result about P0321's Riesz exponent s.

subject: Lewin 2022 Theorem 47 versus Section VI.B
independent_reproduction: Theorem 47 is stated for d in {1,2}, s>d. Section VI.B later discusses two-dimensional s=0 and s=1 numerics. Thus Theorem 47 alone cannot support a translation-invariance assertion for those long-range cases.
source_quote: For d in {1, 2} and s > d
source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.09240 PDF p.60, lines 6850-6851; pp.65-66, lines 7347-7409
gap: This is a scoping correction, not a counterexample to translation invariance for s<=d.

subject: w546/LEMMA_L02.md
independent_reproduction: Half-curl multiplies the transverse spectral projector by |k|^2/4 and annihilates the longitudinal part, giving flat f_theta=1/(4 beta mu). The disk transform is Lambda J1(Lambda r)/(2pi r), so R_theta(0)=Lambda^2/(16pi beta mu) and C6 tends to exp[-9Lambda^2/(4pi beta mu)]. Angular integration of sin^2(phi-alpha)(1-cos(t cos phi)) yields pi[1-J0(t)-cos(2alpha)J2(t)], confirming the J2 sign and eta=|G|^2/(4pi beta mu).
gap: No Riesz Gibbs derivation, defects, or microscopic bond-angle identification.

subject: w546/LEMMA_L03.md
scope: anchored Gaussian field with |k|^-2 angle spectrum
independent_reproduction: The covariance is a finite positive Gram integral because each anchored Fourier factor is O(|k|) at zero. Polar integration gives Var(g(x)-g(0))=F(Lambda r)/(pi beta K). Since 1-J0(t)=O(t^2) near zero and J0(t)/t is integrable at infinity, F(z)=log z+b+o(1). The Gaussian characteristic function gives exponent m^2/(2pi beta K).
gap: This specifies an angular proxy, with no positional or actual Gibbs phase conclusion.

subject: w546/LEMMA_L04.md
independent_reproduction: Given a Gaussian increment delta and uniform fractional offset W/h, randomized rounding has conditional mean delta and variance h^2 t(1-t), t=fractional part(delta/h). Total variance yields v<=Var(q(x)-q(y))<=v+h^2/4; all q differences are hZ-valued, so exp(i6 difference)=1. Conditional uniformity of (V+g(a)) mod h proves joint stationarity of increments without spatial independence.
gap: The abstract quantized field is not a Riesz Gibbs point configuration.

subject: w546/LEMMA_L05.md
scope: smooth monotone bounded perturbation of Gaussian angle lift
independent_reproduction: For delta=g(x)-g(y), uniform W gives zero mean sine correction and conditional variance A^2[1-cos(m delta)]; total variance yields v+A^2[1-exp(-m^2v/2)]. The periodic p(t)=exp(i m f_A(t)) has Fourier autocorrelation sum_n |c_n|^2 exp(-m^2 n^2 v/2), so as v tends to infinity only |c_0|^2 remains. Direct Taylor expansion gives c_0=-mA/2+remainder with |remainder|<=m^2 A^2/4, hence positive plateau for 0<mA<1; the exact Bessel value is J1(mA)^2.
gap: Covariance-only inference is refuted; microscopic Riesz bond correlations and defect theory remain open.
